title.narrative: NLNO Project Commission - Syria 2026 - Humanitarian Integrated Support

description.narrative:
Activity 1.1.1: Provision of Remedial Education Sessions for Vulnerable Children in Homs PIan Syria with its local partner HAND will provide remedial sessions in the targeted schools by HAND trained facilitators to 2400 vulnerable children in Homs to support their education and retention in alignment with the efforts to improve their reintegration. Students will be identified across 6 targeted primary schools by Ministry of Education (MoE) and Directorate of Education (DoE) . The schools will be identified in coordination with theMoE and DoE and relevant Education and Protection sector actors, based on vulnerability criteria including which schools are most vulnerable, have the highest drop out rates, and the most undercovered . All students in the selected schools will receive support as part of this activity. This activity aims to support vulnerable and returnee children in Homs who are at risk of falling behind academically due to disrupted education and limited access to learning resources. This initiative will help bridge learning gaps and improve retention in formal schooling during summer break and before the beginning of the new scholastic year end of 2026 through two cycles of catch-up sessions.
Activity 1.1.2: Commission and distribute education kits to 15 vulnerable primary schools to support students’ learning and reduce barriers to education. In response to the continued impact of the crisis on the education system in Homs, Plan in Syria, in partnership with its local partner HAND, will commission and deliver essential school supplies kits to 15 affected primary schools in the targeted areas. The intervention aims to restore and improve the learning environment for girls and boys with or without disabilities by providing key materials such as whiteboards, markers, A4 paper, toners, seats, and other essential items that enable effective teaching and learning.
Schools will be identified and selected in close coordination with the MoE and DoE as mentioned in Activity 1.1.1, based on agreed criteria of vulnerability and outreach, ensuring that support reaches the most affected and underserved schools. This will strengthen the capacity of schools to deliver safe and quality education, reduce barriers to learning, and help girls and boys regain a sense of normalcy and stability in their education.
Activity 2.1.1: Provide Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) to vulnerable households A total of 100 newly vulnerable and returned households not currently covered by other cash programs will receive MPCA over two consecutive months to help meet their basic and food needs. Households will be selected based on an assessment administered by HAND. Households prioritized will be those with 5+ individuals, those with PwDs or PWSNs, those with no source of income, and those not benefitting from humanitarian assistance from other organisations/initiatives. Each household will receive a payment of 150 USD for a family of 5 individuals, benefitting 500 women, men, girls, and boys, in line with the cash working group Emergency MPC guidance. Beneficiaries will be identified in coordination with local municipalities and the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor. Households will be assessed using a standardized tool, with selection based on socio-economic vulnerability, giving priority to female-headed households, households with persons with disabilities (PwDs), and other marginalized groups. Plan and HAND are committed to vetting and conducting an Anti-Terrorism Screening (ATS) for the selected individuals in accordance with their compliance procedures. The amount will be transferred to the selected individuals through a third-party service provider with whom HAND has an established agreement.
Activity 3.1.1: Conduct GBV awareness, personal hygiene and water conservation sessions targeting women and men to foster community-wide understanding and prevention. Tailored awareness sessions will be conducted with 1,200 men and women in the targeted schools from the targeted communities. by HAND trained facilitators. Participants from diverse backgrounds will have the opportunity to discuss shared challenges, foster mutual respect, and strengthen community collaboration in addressing GBV and other issues. The sessions will cover GBV prevention (core GBV risk-mitigation, referral pathways, basic PSEA messaging, and survivor-centered principles), personal hygiene, and water conservation practices in light of the ongoing drought in Syria. Sessions are small-group (20–25 people), with women-only options and safeguarding protocols. Participants will also receive informational brochures summarizing key messages on GBV prevention and will also be informed about referral mechanisms and pathways to ensure they are referred to needed services.

Education and Assistance Syria continues to experience a steady influx of returnees throughout the year, many of whom face significant challenges in reintegrating into communities that are still recovering from years of conflict. Families are already struggling with the aftermath of displacement, damaged infrastructure, and limited access to basic services. Moreover, many households lack adequate shelter, heating, and resources to endure the cold months. Schools in Homs are under-resourced and ill-equipped to provide a safe and conducive learning environment. They lack essential materials to sustain effective teaching and learning. Among the most pressing needs is access to quality education. Children returning to Syria often face disrupted schooling and limited availability of learning spaces that hinder their ability to stay enrolled. Schools are frequently under-resourced and overwhelmed, struggling to accommodate the growing number of students. In this context, sustained outreach and targeted support are essential to ensure that returnee children are not only enrolled in school but also retained through remedial sessions and support throughout the year.
Women and Protection Women and girls in Homs face serious vulnerabilities, particularly in relation to gender-based violence (GBV), which is pervasive and deeply rooted in patriarchal norms and conflict-related stressors, making it multifaceted. Women report daily experiences of IPV (Intimate Partner Violence), including beatings, verbal abuse, and reproductive coercion. Emotional trauma, depression, and suicidal ideation are common outcomes . Other forms of GBV include sexual harassment, economic violence, early and forced marriage, and denial of access to resources and services. These abuses are driven by insecurity, displacement, economic hardship, and discriminatory social norms that silence women and discourage reporting, especially when custody of children is at stake .
Against this backdrop, this proposed project will provide winterization kits for vulnerable students and essential supplies to underserved schools, alongside multipurpose cash assistance, household hygiene kits, and GBV and hygiene awareness sessions. This multi-sectoral approach aims to help returnees and vulnerable households meet essential needs, promote safe and dignified living conditions, and support community recovery in rural and urban Qusseir areas.

Following the change of authorities in December 2024, Syria remains in a fragile transition marked by insecurity, economic decline, and the effects of the worst drought in 36 years. Despite stabilization efforts, humanitarian needs continue to grow as millions face reduced access to basic services, including education, limited livelihood opportunities, and rising living costs. Over 90% of Syrians live below the poverty line, with families struggling to afford essential food and hygiene items . In Homs Governorate, there has been a record of 140,754 returnees to Homs since December 2024 which placed additional strain on damaged infrastructure and overstretched services. Many households live in unsafe shelters and lack basic supplies, while children face barriers to education and heightened protection risks.

SUMMARY: Following the change of authorities in December 2024, Syria remains in a fragile transition marked by insecurity, economic decline, and the effects of the worst drought in 36 years. Despite stabilization efforts, humanitarian needs continue to grow as millions face reduced access to basic services, including education, limited livelihood opportunities, and rising living costs. Over 90% of Syrians live below the poverty line, with families struggling to afford essential food and hygiene items . Plan International Netherlands, namely Project Commission, approved to contribute to providing a seed-fund for a basic and integrated humanitarian support for the most vulnerable internally displaced and returnees people in Syria.

The project is structured around 3 outcomes:
Outcome 1: School-aged children in vulnerable communities are better equipped to attend and remain in school educational support. Output 1.1: Vulnerable school-aged children receive remedial educational support to reduce hardship and promote school retention, while schools will be provided with education supplies kits to improve the learning environment.
Outcome 2: Vulnerable households have improved financial stability and reduced reliance on negative coping mechanisms through access to cash assistance. Output 2.1: Vulnerable households receive Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) to meet basic needs and reduce negative coping mechanisms.
Outcome 3: Vulnerable households have improved resilience through increased awareness and access to protection information services. Output 3.1 Women and men are better informed about GBV through awareness sessions and are supported to seek protection services when needed.

The project’s intervention and results will generate lasting positive effects within the targeted communities by strengthening resilience, promoting self-reliance, and encouraging sustainable behavioural change. Through the provision of awareness activities, men and women will adopt improved practices that enhance community health and reduce the risk of GBV over time. Women and girls gain confidence to speak out, seek support, and assert their rights. Community members may become advocates for change, helping to protect others. The Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance empowers households to make informed choices based on their priorities, reinforcing autonomy and responsible resource management. Additionally, the distribution of school supply kits supports uninterrupted learning, encouraging consistent school attendance and contributing to better educational outcomes for girls and boys. Remedial sessions support children in catching up on foundational subjects, reducing learning gaps caused by displacement or interrupted schooling. Better performance increases confidence and motivation to stay in school. These interventions respond to immediate needs while cultivating long-term capacities that enable communities to maintain well-being and stability beyond the project’s duration.

• 100 households will receive a payment of 150 USD for a family of 5 individuals, reaching 500 beneficiaries across two rounds over two consecutive months . • 15 affected schools, reaching 40 class equivalents per school through stationery and supplies support • 2400 students will attend remedial sessions • 1,200 men and women will attend awareness sessions
